decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add ... bookmarks (URL, title, description, tags) via a modal form” and “bare domains ... are auto-prefixed”; client round 1: “I can save ... my bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: saving a bookmark by URL conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add / edit ... bookmarks (URL, title, description, tags) via a modal form”; client round 1: “I can ... edit ... my bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the presented form permits title and description entry before saving and editing afterward. Automatic collection is assessed separately.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 explicitly limits editable fields to “URL, title, description, tags,” omitting note; client round 1 gives general approval: “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the editable field set omits the required bookmark note. The client does not identify or explicitly accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents bookmark fields as “URL, title, description, tags” and describes no note entry or rendered markdown view; client round 1: “This does what I need ... I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the explicitly presented bookmark content model lacks markdown notes and their rendered view; bare approval does not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks”; client round 1: “I can ... delete my bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmark deletion conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 includes “tags” in the bookmark form and reports that “tags render as filter chips”; client round 1 says the app lets them “organize” bookmarks.
decisions.note: Implementation review: assigning tags to bookmarks conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Live search across title, URL, description, and tags,” omitting note from the stated searchable fields; client round 1: “I can ... find ... my bookmarks” and approves the app.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the presented full-text search does not cover the required note field. The client does not mention that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Tag filtering ... click a chip (in the bar or on a card) to filter”; client round 1 generally approves the organization and find behavior.
decisions.note: Implementation review: selecting a specific tag to filter bookmarks conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 offers “automatic page-title fetching from the URL” as something that “could [be] add[ed],” establishing that it is absent from the current app; client round 1: “I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation review/feature offer: automatic title collection is missing. The client neither states the expected automatic behavior nor explicitly accepts its absence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 lists “favicons” among features that “could [be] add[ed]”; client round 1 responds only with general satisfaction.
decisions.note: Implementation review/feature offer: automatic favicon collection is absent. Bare approval is not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 mentions bookmark cards and tag chips but identifies “favicons” as a possible future addition; client round 1: “This does what I need ... I’m happy with it as it is.”
decisions.note: Implementation review/feature offer: the list cannot expose the required favicon while favicon support is absent. The client does not surface this difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 offers “import/export (e.g. browser bookmark HTML)” as a possible addition; client round 1 chooses the current app through general approval without mentioning import.
decisions.note: Implementation review/feature offer: Netscape/browser HTML import is not included. The client gives no explicit statement of the missing expectation or difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 offers “import/export (e.g. browser bookmark HTML)” as a possible addition; client round 1 says, “I’m happy with it as it is,” without discussing export.
decisions.note: Implementation review/feature offer: Netscape/browser HTML export is not included. General approval does not qualify as explicit acceptance of the divergence.
